# Supplemental semantic development holdout

Twelve original synthetic dossiers cover the gaps identified by the 0.1.12 rule
traceability review. There are 15 material finding units, plus clean controls and
scope constraints. This is a primary-agent-authored development set, not an
independently authored or human-accepted benchmark.

Copy only targets/ into native host projects. Never copy gold/ or this README into
their model-visible target directory. Each scenario has its own declared scope;
identities must not be joined across scenarios. Both hosts receive identical
target bytes and prompt instructions, differing only in the installed skill path.

The dossiers cover task prerequisites, media equivalents, accurate metadata,
complete/partial internal graphs, supplied raw/rendered differences, accessible
task facts, question coverage, concise answers, duplicate-task preservation,
journey navigation, compatible/incompatible cohorts and structured-data claims.
Media descriptions and rendered DOM are supplied assertions, not actual browser,
pixel or video inspection. No external service or live site is involved.

Gold units consolidate one issue across multiple rule tags. Suggested rules are
labels, not separate true-positive counts. Additional predictions need independent
supported/unsupported adjudication; simply matching all seeded errors is not a
precision result. A source hash binds input bytes, not truth of the supplied facts.
All cases are noncritical in this rubric; the existing critical transport/security
fixtures remain separate and must not be claimed covered by this set.

Retain exact full reports and tool traces for evaluation. Assess clean controls,
scope overreach, quotation fidelity, invented metrics and final-summary consistency
as well as finding recall. Freeze target bytes and gold before native execution;
do not edit them to fit a model response after seeing its output.
